On the first beat he snaps the fanned brick of notes shut and taps it on the table; on the next he fans it open again toward the lens with a flourish, head cocked; then he pats the pile twice with his flat glove like a proud drummer, shoulders bouncing, and leans forward over the stacks, chin up. He keeps the same brick in his hand the whole time; the stacks stay put. Mask, gloves and suit never change. No speech; paper riffle, thumps on wood.

Thanks.
